title: Japan national CPI (October 2026), 08:30 JST — the comparator the November print decelerates against
source: EST: two independent Statistics Bureau surfaces, both fetched and parsed by this session on 2026-09-05. (1) stat.go.jp/english/data/cpi/1582.html ('Consumer Price Index — Schedule of Release', HTTP 200, 13,839 bytes), whose single 17-row table parses row-by-row against the header 'Japan: Survey month | Date of release || Ku-area of Tokyo (preliminary): Survey month | Date of release || Remarks' as ['October', 'November 20', 'November', 'November 27', ''] — i.e. the October-2026 national CPI releases 2026-11-20. (2) stat.go.jp/data/kouhyou/e-stat_cpi.xml, the Bureau's own machine-readable 公表予定 feed (HTTP 200, 59,990 bytes, UTF-16LE), linked from its live Japanese results page and carrying its own update stamp of 2026-08-28 — eight days before this fetch. Its 全国 class lists '2026-11-20 08:30 | 2026年10月分'. THE 08:30 JST RELEASE TIME IS READ OFF THAT FEED, not asserted from convention: every one of the feed's 37 scheduled items carries release_hour 08 and release_minute 30. Filed estimate on two counts only — the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has BLS:/BEA:/CENSUS: for US statistical agencies and no slot for Japan's Statistics Bureau, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. NOTE that the usual third count does not apply here: the staleness objection other Japan CPI entries carry (the English page's own 'Last Update : 23 January 2026') is answered by the XML feed, which was re-published 2026-08-28 and agrees with the English table on all 30 release dates.
notes: DISCOVERED during the japan-cpi-2026-12-18 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05), and tracked for one specific reason rather than for completeness: it is the COMPARATOR that FT-japan-cpi-2026-12-18-1 scores against. That test predicts the November-2026 national core y/y (released 2026-12-18) prints at or below the October-2026 core y/y released on THIS date, on seasonal-base arithmetic. The grounds, computed by that lane from the Bureau's own 2025-base national monthly file (e-Stat statInfId=000040491314, fileKind=4, parsed locally out of the OOXML, 679 observations 1970-01 to 2026-07): the 2025 all-items index path runs 99.3, 98.9, 99.2, 99.7, 100.0, 99.9, 100.1, 100.3, 100.1, 100.7, 101.0, 100.9 — NOVEMBER IS THE CALENDAR-YEAR PEAK, on the BoJ's core measure (101.1) as well as the headline. Against the 2015-2024 seasonal norm, 2025's Oct-to-Nov month-over-month was +0.298% all-items versus a norm of -0.004% (a +0.30pp HARD base) and +0.397% core versus +0.118% (+0.28pp), reversing to an easy base the following month. So a seasonally normal November-2026 prints roughly 0.3pp below whatever lands on this date — which makes this release the number that determines whether that test passes. The excess base on core-core is only +0.01pp, the tell that the effect is a fresh-food-and-energy base rather than an underlying turn. Impact is LOW: symbols is empty and no house playbook is keyed to Japanese CPI; this entry's value is scoring and attribution, not a trade. Two further dated facts from the same primaries, recorded so the next session does not re-fetch them: the Tokyo November flash follows on 2026-11-27 at 08:30 JST (tracked separately as japan-cpi-tokyo-flash-2026-11-27), and this date is a Friday with NO Bank of Japan meeting — 28 of the Bureau's 30 scheduled release dates are Fridays, the two exceptions being Tuesdays in March.
